title: burst-pacing-econ-scan-annotated-notes
content:
Goal:
Quick annotated readout of burst-pacing experiments: understand how several pacing/windowing strategies change (1) p50/p90/p99 token latency, (2) $/1M tokens, and (3) burst-resilience when session arrivals spike. This is meant as a short working memo for product + platform to decide which knobs to expose in the Console Optimize tab (prefetch window, soft quota, burst-sculpting).

Summary (high level, tl;dr):
- Pacing windows (time-bucket based warmup) + active prefetch gives the best median latency at modest cost increase for short bursts (<=15s).
- For extreme microbursts (sustained QPS x3 for >60s) adaptive-slot-allocation with slot preemption kept p99 20–30% lower than naive fixed-pool, but cost increased ~12%.
- Smallbatch (max-batch 2) reduces p50 by ~15% for chat-style TTL workloads but increases overall CPU/GPU utilization inefficiency; effective only when combined with prefix caching.
- Recommendation: expose two presets in Console: "burst-friendly" (pacing window=10s, prefetch=on, soft-quota=20%) and "steady-econ" (no prefetch, prioritized packing).

Experimental setup (notes / reproducibility):
- Model: redwood-v2-13b-8bit (quant profile q3), seq_len=1024 typical; responses mean 64 tokens.
- Runtime: Dedicated pool (A100 equivalent nodes), 16 nodes in core pool, max burstable pool +8 nodes.
- Workloads simulated via trace-replayer (sessionized): baseline arrival process = poisson with lambda tuned for 200 qps steady; bursts injected as sudden 3x/5x multipliers of differing durations (5s, 20s, 60s).
- Key knobs varied: pacing-window (0s, 5s, 10s, 30s), prefetch (off/on), soft-quota fraction (0%, 10%, 20%), smallbatch threshold (1,2,4), kv-cache-ttl (3m, 15m).
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 token latency (client-observed), tail-penalty (% requests > SLA), amortized cost ($ per 1M tokens) computed from node-hour consumption + GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.

Representative results (annotated text charts):
- Scenario A: short burst (3x for 10s)
  * pacing-window=0s, prefetch=off: p50=42ms, p90=210ms, p99=820ms, cost=$120 /1M tokens, tail-penalty=7%
  * pacing-window=10s, prefetch=on: p50=36ms, p90=170ms, p99=450ms, cost=$138 /1M tokens (+15%), tail-penalty=2%
  * pacing-window=30s, prefetch=on: p50=40ms, p90=195ms, p99=500ms, cost=$155 /1M tokens (+29%), tail-penalty=2.5%

- Scenario B: microburst prolonged (5x for 60s)
  * fixed-pool, pacing=0: p50=50ms, p90=310ms, p99=1100ms, cost=$210 /1M tokens, many preemption events
  * adaptive-slot (preemption allowed, soft-quota=20%): p50=46ms, p90=260ms, p99=780ms, cost=$236 /1M tokens (+12%), fewer SLA misses
  * smallbatch=2 + prefix-caching: p50=38ms, p90=230ms, p99=700ms, cost=$248 /1M tokens (+18%), but GPU occupancy decreased 6%

ASCII mini-plot (p99 vs cost for short burst sweep):
  p99-ms | cost-$per-1M   (lower-left is better)
  -------------------------------------------
  820    | 120   (no pacing)
  500    | 155   (pacing=30s,prefetch)
  450    | 138   (pacing=10s,prefetch)

Observations / interpretation (working):
- Diminishing returns: increasing pacing beyond 10s gives smaller tail reductions but increasing cost fairly linearly; 10s looks like a knee for common chat bursts.
- Prefetch trade: helps p90/p99 much more than p50, because it reduces cold-start penalties on short-lived sessions. But prefetch increases sustained resource commitment; for customers with flat sustained load this is wasteful.
- Smallbatch is a double-edged sword: great for bursty low-latency interactions when prefix overlap is high (KV hit>60%) but harmful when sessions are diverse (cache hit <40%) because it fragments GPU batches and reduces utilization.
- Soft-quota preemption is useful when customer SLAs permit a fraction of requests to be deprioritized; it acts like "graceful degradation" and reduces p99 by avoiding massive queue buildup.

Cost accounting caveats (short-hand):
- Our $/1M tokens includes amortized node-hours for burst capacity (we charged burst nodes at on-demand rate with 95% utilization for the burst window) + ~10% infra overhead (networking/software). This is surface-level — finance will need bucketed pricing if we expose presets.
- For Dedicated customers with reserved capacity, incremental cost of burst knobs is mostly operational (lost packing efficiency) rather than raw node-hour billing.

Stitching to Console UX (notes to product):
- Propose two user-facing toggles for beta: 1) "Burst Sculpt" preset picker (burst-friendly, steady-econ, cost-saver), 2) "Prefetch intensity" slider (off/low/high maps to prefetch TTL & count). Default for new tenants: steady-econ.
- Instrumentation hooks required: per-tenant KV cache-hit, per-tenant prefetch success rate, tail-penalty heatmap by minute. Add these to Console Console -> Optimize usage page.

Open questions & followups (todo):
- Run same sweep with multi-model mix (embedding + generation) to observe interference; current runs are single-model only. (owner: Owen)
- Evaluate prefetch safety for private deployments (HSM/KMS constraints) — do we need policy gating? (security review request: JIRA-SEC-688)
- Need a microbenchmark for prefix similarity: how correlated are session prefixes in real tenant traces? If correlation <50% prefetch harms more than helps. (data ask: Lina)

Raw notes / scraps (for later cleaning):
- observed odd spike around 23:14 in one run — looks like allocator churn + GC in runtime; add more tracing. Ticketed as JIRA-PLAT-5249.
- customer anecdote: onboarding chat app saw p99 halved after enabling prefetch but cost up ~20% — aligns with our short-burst result (useful for marketing collateral).

Quick recommendation (one-liner to share):
Offer a "burst-friendly" preset that is explicit about a ~10–20% cost premium in exchange for 50–70% improvement in p99 for short bursts; provide telemetry to let customers toggle back when their session prefix correlations are low.

Appendix: short checklist before slide-deck
- run multi-model interference sweep (priority: high)
- compute more conservative cost buckets for reserved capacity customers
- add per-tenant prefix-correlation metric + thresholding logic
- prepare Console mockups for two presets + telemetry panel

-- end of draft --

Notes to self: keep this concise for now, will expand into a one-pager for product review.
